title: Grade 4 SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — General Assessment #7

pages.quiz:
SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #7
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KPSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which change is a physical change? (1 mark)
   A. Milk souring
   B. Iron rusting
   C. Paper burning to ash
   D. Ice melting to water

2. Soil erosion is reduced by: (1 mark)
   A. Planting cover crops and terracing slopes
   B. Removing all vegetation
   C. Overgrazing continuously
   D. Burning crop residue every week

3. Why is water unsuitable for a petrol fire? (1 mark)
   A. Water removes heat too quickly
   B. Petrol fires have no fuel
   C. Water always increases oxygen
   D. Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely

4. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. Heating until a solid melts
   B. Movement of water only across a membrane
   C. A chemical reaction forming ash
   D. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration

5. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio
   B. A compound can be separated by filtering only
   C. A mixture always has a fixed melting point
   D. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya

6. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Properties of Matter? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Properties of Matter.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Properties of Matter.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Properties of Matter.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Properties of Matter.

7. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 0 °C
   B. 37 °C
   C. 100 °C
   D. 50 °C

8. Photosynthesis mainly produces: (1 mark)
   A. Nitrogen gas only
   B. Only water vapour
   C. Glucose and oxygen
   D. Only carbon dioxide

9. The SI unit of force is the: (1 mark)
   A. newton (N)
   B. pascal (Pa)
   C. watt (W)
   D. joule (J)

10. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Light? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Light.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Light.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Light.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Light.

11. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Heat? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Heat.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Heat.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Heat.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Heat.

12. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means
   B. Any substance that conducts electricity
   C. Any white crystal used in cooking
   D. A mixture of two liquids

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Water Conservation and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Light and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Heat and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Properties of Matter and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
MARKING SCHEME
====

1. D — Ice melting to water

2. A — Planting cover crops and terracing slopes

3. D — Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely

4. D — Net movement of particles from high to low concentration

5. A — Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio

6. A — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Properties of Matter.

7. C — 100 °C

8. C — Glucose and oxygen

9. A — newton (N)

10. D — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Light.

11. A — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Heat.

12. A — A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means

16. (4 marks)
